correctness.rationale: The exact positive AN characterization is singleton essential spectrum {β} plus finite-rank below-β spectral projection. Calkin quotient contractivity gives ||A−B||≥||π(A)−β1||=max(|m−β|,|M−β|)≥(M−m)/2, uniquely optimized at β=c=(m+M)/2. For ε>0 the subspace Pε=E_A([0,m−ε)) is finite-rank (any spectrum bounded away from the essential bottom consists of finitely many isolated finite-multiplicity eigenvalues). The commuting spectral clipping Bε=A Pε+[cI+(A−MI)_+](I−Pε) is positive, with positive excess compact and negative excess finite-rank, hence AN; ||A−Bε||≤δ+ε. If the full below-m projection P is finite-rank, the same formula attains δ. Conversely a δ-best B must have essential scalar c; its below-c projection Q is finite-rank, so if E_A([0,m)) infinite-dimensional choose unit x in it orthogonal to Q, giving <Bx,x>≥c and <Ax,x><m; thus ||A−B||>c−m=δ. The strict spectral expectation holds even if eigenvalues accumulate at m. Border m=M including m=M=0 follows from the same argument. Independently verified diagonal counterexample: alternate eigenvalues 1−1/(k+1), 2+1/(k+1) have m=1,M=2, infinite below-m subspace and unattained inf 1/2; replacing lows by 1+1/(k+1) makes the best operator attainable.
residual_risks: Only positive approximants, not entire AN class.
Strongest non-elementary imported ingredient is positive AN spectral characterization; no false formal independence claimed.

value.rationale: The distance-to-class and attainment/proximinality dichotomy are basic approximation geometry of the positive operator cone; explicit essential-spectrum clipping provides both quantitative distance and a structural obstruction to nearest points. Correctness alone would not confer value, but the precise infinite-dimensional gap between arbitrary approximation and exact minimization is an independently useful classification beyond membership and closure.
residual_risks: Does not address nonpositive AN approximants or uniqueness of minimizers.

final_claim: For any bounded positive self-adjoint operator A on any infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, its distance to positive absolutely norm-attaining operators is half the width (M−m)/2 of its essential spectrum, and a nearest positive AN operator exists iff E_A([0,m)) has finite rank; an explicit positive spectral clipping attains the distance in that case.
limitations: Results are for bounded positive operators on complex Hilbert spaces, not arbitrary AN operators.
No uniqueness of nearest point is claimed.
